meta.title: From a custom implementation
meta.description: Mapping a hand-written shift board onto this one: items, levels, shifts, strings and styles.

who.intro: You already have a schedule on screen. Somebody wrote it — a list grouped by shift, or a column of cards with absolute positions — and it works, but every new requirement lands on the same few hundred lines. This guide maps what you have onto what this package already does.
points: You render a day, or a shift, as a list or as a time grid.
You have your own idea of severity, priority or status, and it decides colors and order.
You have handled at least one of: items that overlap, a shift that crosses midnight, items that must stay in view once they scroll past.
You are on React 18.2 or 19 and can add a dependency.

summary.intro: What moves, and what it becomes. Nothing here needs a codemod: the change is a mapping function and a few props.
rows: Map it once; keep your own object in data.
One definition per key: rank, color, card treatment, whether it pins.
An anchor and a length. The component decides which shift is current.
Delete it. The cap and the promotion are built in.
Set pinOnPass on the levels that belong there.
Pass one of the seven, or write your own object.
Start with the tokens; reach for slots only where the structure has to differ.
Keep yours if it is doing work; the prop hands it the item.

items.title: Map your rows to items
items.text: An item needs an id, a start and a title. Everything else is optional, and your own object rides along in data, typed, so slots and handlers can reach it without a lookup.

levels.title: Turn your severity into levels
levels.text: A level definition is what decides color, order and card treatment. Give the strongest the lowest rank. If your scale is close to the classic nine, start from classicLevels and edit; if it is not, define your own — nothing in the component assumes the classic keys.

shifts.title: Describe the day instead of grouping it
shifts.text: Rather than bucketing items yourself, say how long a shift is and when one of them starts. The component places every item, decides which shift holds the current moment, and renders the ones before and after it. A shift that crosses midnight needs nothing extra.

strings.title: Move your strings into a locale pack
strings.text: Every string the component shows comes from one object. Pass one of the seven packs, or spread one and replace the messages you word differently. Your own strings — the titles of your items — stay yours.

styles.title: Rebuild the look with tokens first
styles.text: Most house styles are a handful of CSS variables: a surface, a radius, an accent. Set those before writing any CSS of your own, then use classNames for the rules that remain, and slots only where the markup itself has to be different.

behavior.title: Replace your interception points
behavior.text: A confirmation before opening, a permission check, an unsaved-changes prompt: those become middleware. A handler runs before the component acts and can cancel it, so the component keeps its own state machine and you keep your rules.

removed.text: Nothing yet. This is the first release, so there is no rename or removal to carry. Every later change of that kind is recorded in the <link to="/discover-more/changelog/">Changelog</link>, and one that needs steps gets a guide of its own next to this one.
